Record Class PlayerStatsDTO

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
it.polimi.ingsw.am56.network.message.classesDTO.PlayerStatsDTO
Record Components:
nickname - the player's nickname
color - the player's totem colour
food - the player's current food
points - the player's current victory points
collectorCards - card ids of the player's Collector character cards
hunterCards - card ids of the player's Hunter character cards
builderCards - card ids of the player's Builder character cards
shamanCards - card ids of the player's Shaman character cards
artistCards - card ids of the player's Artist character cards
inventorCards - card ids of the player's Inventor character cards
feedingSale - cumulative feeding discount the player has accrued
buildingSale - cumulative building-purchase discount the player has accrued
shamanStars - the player's shaman-stars total
inventionCount - number of distinct inventions the player has discovered
canPickUpper - whether the player may still pick a card from the upper row this turn
canPickLower - whether the player may still pick a card from the lower row this turn
affordableBuildingIds - card ids of the board buildings the player can currently afford (food at least the cost minus buildingSale)
ownedBuildingCards - card ids of the building cards the player already owns
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public record PlayerStatsDTO(String nickname, String color, int food, int points, List<Integer> collectorCards, List<Integer> hunterCards, List<Integer> builderCards, List<Integer> shamanCards, List<Integer> artistCards, List<Integer> inventorCards, int feedingSale, int buildingSale, int shamanStars, int inventionCount, boolean canPickUpper, boolean canPickLower, List<Integer> affordableBuildingIds, List<Integer> ownedBuildingCards) extends Record implements Serializable
Transport snapshot of a single player's in-game state. The character hand is sent as one id list per archetype (rather than counts) so the client can render the actual cards, and the affordability / pick flags are pre-computed server-side so the views don't need to re-derive the rules.
